work.permit: Prethodno odobrenje tijela nadležnog za poslove socijalne skrbi

note: Majority: the Family Act (Obiteljski zakon, NN 103/15 as amended), article 117(3): a person of eighteen is of age; a court may let a 16-year-old marry (article 25), which isn't held. Work: the Labour Act (Zakon o radu, NN 93/14 as amended to NN 151/22), article 19: a person under fifteen, or of 15 to 18 still in compulsory primary schooling, may not be employed; article 20 lets a minor of fifteen sign an employment contract with the legal representative's written authorisation. Article 19.a(5): a child or minor in compulsory schooling may take paid part in filming, advertising, artistic, stage or similar cultural works and sports competitions only with the prior approval of the social welfare authority; no lower age is set. Hours limits aren't held. Service: the Act amending the Defence Act (Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o obrani, NN 136/2025, passed 24 October 2025, in force on the eighth day after publication on 5 November 2025) reintroduces basic military training for male conscripts (article 21(2)); women are not conscripted. Recruits are sent in the calendar year they turn 19 (article 21.n(1)), older ones up to the end of their 30th year (article 21.n(3)); the form holds 19 to 30, reading 'do isteka 30 godina života' as reaching 30. Training lasts two months (article 21.m(2)); civil service instead lasts three or four months, as the Ministry of Defence's page says. Registration at 18 isn't held. Texts read from zakon.hr (a private legal database's consolidated text, as of NN 110/26) and the official gazette (Narodne novine).
